question: Ugadi falls in the first month of the Hindu calendar called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ugadi, also known as Yugadi, marks the **New Year in the Hindu lunar calendar** and is primarily celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
 
• The festival falls in the first month of the Hindu calendar, which is called **Chaitra**, according to the lunisolar system.
 
• Chaitra is the first month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar, and Ugadi is observed on the first day of the waxing phase of the moon (Shukla Paksha) in this month.
 
• Ugadi symbolizes the beginning of a new era and is associated with the **spring season**, signifying prosperity, growth, and new beginnings.
 
• The festival is celebrated with traditions such as **preparing Ugadi Pachadi**, a dish made with six different tastes symbolizing various emotions of life, and decorating homes with mango leaves and rangoli.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vaishakha**
 
 
• Vaishakha is the second month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar and follows Chaitra.
 
• It typically overlaps with April and May in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Vaishakha is associated with several festivals, including **Akshaya Tritiya** and Buddha Purnima.
 
 
 
• **Magha**
 
 
• Magha is the eleventh month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar.
 
• It corresponds to January-February in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The month is significant for its religious observances such as **Magha Purnima** and the Kumbh Mela held every twelve years.
 
 
 
• **Kartika**
 
 
• Kartika is the eighth month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar.
 
• It typically overlaps with October and November in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The month is considered highly auspicious, with festivals such as **Kartik Purnima** and Diwali being observed during this period.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Ugadi**
 
 
• Ugadi is celebrated as the beginning of a new year and is a time for introspection, renewal, and hope.
 
• The festival reflects the cultural and agricultural significance of the region, marking the end of the harvest season and the onset of the spring season.
